title.description: Full report title: '{Core Pattern} — A Classic Grounded Theory of {Generalized Population}'

abstract.description: ~200 word self-contained summary. Core pattern, core category, population, contribution, implications.

heading.description: Section heading adapted to object_of_study: 'Core Concern', 'Core Emotion', 'Core Behavior', etc.

pattern_identification.description: The label that names the core pattern. Explanation of what the pattern IS and why this label captures it.

emergence_narrative.description: How the pattern emerged from the data. Convergence across documents, key discovery moments, evolution of understanding.

evidential_anchoring.description: Strongest data incidents and codes supporting the pattern. Variation in how participants experience it. Trace to specific nodes/incidents.

heading.description: Always 'Core Category' — this is a formal CGT construct, not adapted to object_of_study.

definition.description: Precise conceptual definition of the core category. What it IS, not what it does (that goes in the model).

properties.description: Properties of the core category, each with its dimensional range.

description.description: What this property captures about the core category.

dimensional_range.description: The range of variation observed for this property (e.g., 'low to high intensity', 'narrow to broad scope').

relationship_to_core_pattern.description: How this category processes, resolves, or addresses the core pattern. The explanatory link between Sections 2 and 3.

model_overview.description: Narrative summary of the full theoretical model. How conditions, strategies, and consequences interconnect through the core category.

conditions.description: Antecedent and structural conditions that shape how the core category operates. Causal and contextual conditions from nodes with entity_type 'condition'.

core_process.description: The central PROCESSES edge: how the core category processes/resolves the core pattern. This is the obligatory spine of the model. Must be derived from the PROCESSES edge in the input.

strategies.description: Behavioral and cognitive strategies participants employ. Derived from nodes with entity_type 'strategy' and IS_A_STRATEGY_FOR edges.

consequences.description: Outcomes and results, both intended and unintended. Derived from nodes with entity_type 'consequence' and IS_A_CONSEQUENCE_OF edges.

relational_architecture.description: Structured listing of all theoretical relationships (edges). PROCESSES edge MUST be first. Organized by relationship type.

narrative.description: One-sentence narrative of the relationship in conceptual present tense.

population_profile.description: The generalized population to which the theory applies. Abstract enough for transferability, specific enough to be meaningful.

dimensional_variations.description: How the core pattern and core category manifest differently across population dimensions. Document the range of variation, not just central tendency.

scope_boundaries.description: Where the theory does NOT apply. Populations, contexts, or conditions excluded. Honest scope assessment.

emergent_fit_assessment.description: Global evaluation: does the theory genuinely dialogue with literature, or is it forced to fit? Candid assessment.

extends.description: Where the literature confirms and the theory extends existing knowledge with new properties, dimensions, or relationships.

modifies.description: Where the literature suggests modifications to received concepts, and how the emergent theory revises them.

integrates.description: Where the theory unifies scattered concepts from the literature into a coherent explanatory framework.

transcends.description: What the theory reveals that the literature had not captured. The novel contribution of this grounded theory.

control_variables.description: Aspects of the phenomenon that can be modified in practice. Each traces to a theoretical property.

description.description: What can be modified and how.

theory_basis.description: Which theoretical property or relationship justifies this as modifiable.

access_variables.description: Conditions that enable or constrain intervention.

conditions_access.description: How this variable enables or constrains access to the control variables.

target.description: Who acts on this guideline (e.g., practitioner, organization, participant).

mechanism.description: How the guideline produces change, traced to a theoretical mechanism.

practical_limitations.description: What the theory does NOT support in terms of intervention. Guard against over-application.

open_questions.description: Theoretical questions the current data cannot answer. Properties needing further dimensionalization.

why_unresolved.description: Why current data cannot resolve this question (insufficient variation, undersampled dimension, etc.).

methodological_limitations.description: Limitations inherent to study design, sampling, or analytical choices. Candid self-assessment.

future_directions.description: Concrete next studies, populations to sample, comparisons to pursue.

rationale.description: Why this direction emerges from the theory's current gaps or open questions.
